source_window.dataset_title: Opening property extents created from OS MasterMap Topography Layer
source_window.license: Open Government Licence policy context for qualifying PSGA-published extents

field_evidence.policy_effective_date: From 1 July 2020 PSGA members may publish property extents created from OS MasterMap Topography Layer under Open Government Licence terms.
field_evidence.authoritative_publishers_examples: The page gives HM Land Registry and Registers of Scotland INSPIRE polygon datasets as examples of PSGA-member property extents.
field_evidence.property_extent_semantics: Property extents are closed polygons representing real-world or inferred boundary features.
field_evidence.legal_boundary_limitation: OS MasterMap Topography Layer shows physical features on the ground at the time of survey; it never shows legal property boundaries and does not show ownership of physical features.
field_evidence.os_nonpublication_reason: OS states it does not publish its own property-extents dataset under OGL because such data could be mistaken for authoritative legal extent and misused.
field_evidence.identifier_linkage: The page encourages associating TOIDs or UPRNs with property extents, but identifiers do not themselves establish legal parcel geometry.
field_evidence.target_binding: No target-specific authoritative property extent from an eligible publisher is explicitly bound to a verified BUILDING_PRESENT producer record in this lineage.

first_missing_criterion: Verified BUILDING_PRESENT canonical parcel geometry/bbox for this producer. Ordnance Survey's official property-extents guidance states that OS MasterMap Topography Layer shows physical features on the ground but never legal property boundaries or ownership. It also explains that authoritative property extents may instead be published by PSGA members such as HM Land Registry under OGL terms. No target-specific authoritative parcel/title polygon is bound to a verified BUILDING_PRESENT producer record in this lineage. Local OpenCode must perform that target-specific binding; after that, bind one exact official DEM/LIDAR tile or metadata-index record to the resulting bbox.
exact_blocker: The method materially changed from sampling an unmatched HM Land Registry-derived title-boundary polygon to an Ordnance Survey policy/semantics check on whether OS large-scale topography can serve as canonical parcel geometry. OS explicitly states that OS MasterMap Topography Layer shows physical features at survey time and never legal property boundaries or ownership, and that OS itself does not publish a property-extents dataset under OGL because doing so could be mistaken for authoritative legal extent. Therefore OS topographic polygons cannot be substituted for a canonical parcel/title polygon. The verified lineage still lacks a target-bound authoritative parcel geometry for BUILDING_PRESENT; spatial join/materialization remains local OpenCode work.
